problem: Object Goal Navigation methods (RL policies, semantic maps like ANS/SemExp) treat each episode independently, and reusing stored semantic maps needs a relocation mechanism or assumes perfect localization (e.g. SMNet). Knowledge learned in earlier episodes of the same environment is not reused.
motivation: Real agents should accumulate and reuse knowledge of environments they have already visited. A compact, semantically rich, grounded symbolic model with visual features can support relocation and cross-episode reuse, and can mitigate noisy segmentation, since objects seen from many states are less likely to be false positives.
key_idea: Incrementally learn a finite-state Abstract Model of each environment (states = Taskonomy visual features + visible object classes + estimated object positions), store it, and reload and merge it via feature-based state matching when the agent recognizes a previously visited place, to guide OGN.
insight: Incremental online learning of Abstract Models beats reusing models pre-explored offline. Ablation: SI 0.279 SR / 0.131 SPL vs SP 0.258 / 0.117, since episodes starting from different locations cover areas a single long pre-exploration misses. The Soft strategy (search around the stored goal position) beats Hard (0.258 vs 0.251 SR) because matches are imperfect. Failure analysis shows most failures come from segmentation errors (Detection), not from the model, and a better exploration policy (SemExp) yields better Abstract Models.
method: Knowledge Extraction: RedNet segments the RGB-D frame, a SLAM-style Map Builder makes an egocentric map, and a State Creator builds abstract state <F_s (Taskonomy autoencoder feature, 2048-d), C_s (object classes), F_{s,c} (map position, bbox, distance)>.
Knowledge Modeling: adds new states and transitions (s_prev, a, s) to the current finite state machine and extends the global map at each step.

Reasoning: if the model contains a state with the goal class, choose the goal among the top-5 most-viewed instances (closest one); otherwise use the ANS/SemExp Global Policy (PPO-trained) to pick an exploration goal; plan with Fast Marching.
Abstract Model Reuse (relocation): match the current state to stored models by cosine distance on F_s (threshold 0.3); on a match, merge the new model into the matched one and rescale coordinates.
Hard vs Soft strategy: Hard blindly trusts the stored goal position; Soft searches an area around it (size proportional to distance from the matched state) and stops early if a goal is seen en route.
Variants: ANS*+HP and ANS*+SP (pre-explored with 10000 steps, Hard/Soft), ANS*+SI (Soft, incremental across episodes), SemExp*+SI (SI on top of SemExp).

setting.backbone: ANS/SemExp-style modular pipeline: RedNet segmentation (pretrained), Taskonomy encoder (frozen), PPO-trained 5-conv Global Policy, Fast Marching planner
setting.training_data: Global Policy trained 10M steps with PPO on 56 Matterport3D training scenes; RedNet pretrained on 40 MP3D classes; Taskonomy encoder pretrained
setting.action_space: low-level: move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left/right 30°, stop (500-step budget, 1 m success threshold)
setting.privileged: none for SI; the pre-explored variants (HP/SP) use Abstract Models built with 10000 exploration steps per environment; pose given as relative odometry

results: Reusing Abstract Models improves OGN: ANS*+SI reaches 27.9 SR / 13.1 SPL vs ANS* 24.0 / 10.2 on MP3D val. SemExp*+SI reaches 34.7 SR, far above SMNet (9.6 SR) and comparable to SMNet(GT) (31.2 SR), which uses GT free-space maps and assumes known absolute position. Relocation succeeded in 69.7% of episodes.
limitations: Relies on noisy semantic segmentation (RedNet); Detection errors are the majority of failures and can cause semantic drift or hallucinated goals.
With-memory setting needs a sequence of episodes in the same environments; without memory the Abstract Model adds little over semantic maps.
Absolute success rates are low (about 28-35%), and the evaluation covers only Matterport3D in simulation, with a hand-set matching threshold.
